label: TP
reason: Alert 2 (java/path-injection) is alert-TP: user input from request.queryString flows through URL decoding and Thing.doSomething() into 'bar', which is concatenated with TESTFILES_DIR to create 'fileName' used in FileOutputStream. This allows path traversal attacks (e.g., ../../../etc/passwd). Alert 1 (java/xss) is alert-FP: the sink expression at L83-L84 calls encodeForHTML(fileName), which encodes the entire fileName (including user portion) before printing to writer, neutralizing XSS in the HTML response.

evidence.note: User input flows from getQueryString() -> substring -> URLDecoder.decode -> Thing.doSomething() -> bar -> fileName (concatenated with TESTFILES_DIR), then fileName is HTML-encoded before print
